title: Production Evidence Receipt
description: Claims payload of a dated, scoped, issuer-signed statement about what an AdCP implementation was observed doing. It is NOT a conformance result, a certification, or a trust decision, and it carries no spend, price, campaign, client, or counterparty identity unless the named party consented. The receipt defines claims only: it is delivered and signed through the existing AttestationReference primitive (claim_type https://adcontextprotocol.org/claims/production-evidence), not through a second signing envelope, and evaluators remain verifier-of-record under their own trust policy. evidence_tier is a ladder, but independence is declared and checkable rather than advisory: the issuer MUST declare every role it played in issuer_counterparty_roles, and at evidence_tier independently_interoperable or above it MUST also declare counterparty_relation and publish an issuance_policy, and a non-empty role declaration requires a structurally independent co-signer. An empty declaration is the issuer's own claim, not proof; evaluators back it with their own accepted-issuer policy. Tiers below conformance_passed (declared, schema_validated) are declarative registry metadata and are not receipts. Experimental in 3.3: shape may change under the experimental-status contract.

receipt_id.description: Issuer-scoped identifier of this receipt. Unique only together with the complete issuer identity. Referenced by supersedes on a later receipt.

claim_type.description: Claim vocabulary URI. Binds the payload to the AttestationReference that delivers it.

issuer.description: The party that observed the activity and signs this receipt. The identity is a claim; evaluators match it against their own trust policy.

subject.description: The implementation the receipt is about. Normally an agent subject (the observed endpoint); a brand subject covers an operator. The issuer MUST NOT be the subject at evidence_tier independently_interoperable or above.

adcp_version.description: Release-precision AdCP version observed on the wire (for example 3.2 or 3.3-beta.1). The receipt is evidence for this release only.

build_version.description: Optional exact build_version the subject reported in get_adcp_capabilities at observation time.

transport.description: Transport over which the activity was observed. A receipt for one transport says nothing about the other.

environment.description: Where the observed activity ran. sandbox is account-flagged test traffic; controlled_pilot is real systems under a bounded, pre-agreed pilot; production is ordinary live traffic. Constrained by evidence_tier.

enumDescriptions.conformance_passed: The subject passed the AdCP storyboard conformance harness for the stated version and transport against a sandbox or test deployment.
enumDescriptions.sandbox_interoperable: The subject completed the stated tasks against a counterparty implementation in sandbox. The counterparty may be the issuer's own or the protocol team's.
enumDescriptions.independently_interoperable: The subject interoperated with a counterparty implementation that is not the subject's, not the protocol team's, and declared independent in counterparty_relation, in sandbox or a controlled pilot. Subject to the independence rules.
enumDescriptions.production_transacted: At least one production MediaBuy was accepted by the subject through the stated task set. Subject to the independence rules. Production alone does not establish an independent counterparty; read counterparty_relation.
enumDescriptions.production_delivered_reconciled: A production MediaBuy reached non-zero delivery, reporting was read back, and reconciliation completed. Subject to the independence rules.

evidence_tier.description: Position on the evidence ladder. Ordered as listed. This is evidence about what was observed, not a grade, and it is separate from conformance grading (AAO Verified).

channels.description: Channels in which the observed activity occurred. The claim does not extend to unlisted channels.

tasks_exercised.description: Canonical AdCP task names the subject successfully completed during the observation. The claim covers exactly this set.

lifecycle_stages_reached.description: Lifecycle stages the observed activity reached. Stages are facts about the observation, not weights.

observation.description: Coarse temporal and volume scope of the observation. Exact counts are deliberately not representable.

first_observed_date.description: UTC calendar date of the first observation. Day granularity on purpose: exact timestamps combined with a coarse band could identify a transaction in a counterparty's logs.

last_observed_date.description: UTC calendar date of the last observation. MUST NOT be before first_observed_date or after the date of issued_at.

activity_band.description: Coarse band of distinct transactions observed at the stated tier. Bands avoid disclosing volume while keeping one-off runs distinguishable from sustained activity.

capability_response_digest.description: Optional digest of the get_adcp_capabilities response the issuer observed, so a later reader can tell which declaration the evidence was gathered against.

audit_record_digest.description: Digest of the issuer's private audit record for this observation. The record itself is retained by the issuer and disclosed only under the consent in publication; the digest lets an auditor later prove which record this receipt summarizes.

enumDescriptions.independent: The counterparty(ies) the subject transacted or interoperated with are not the subject's operator, affiliates, or accounts it controls, and not the protocol team.
enumDescriptions.affiliated: At least one counterparty is the subject's operator, an affiliate, or an account it controls (for example a self-buy).
enumDescriptions.unknown: The issuer cannot determine the relationship.

counterparty_relation.description: The issuer's determination of how the subject relates to the counterparty it interoperated or transacted with. REQUIRED at independently_interoperable and above. independently_interoperable requires independent. Production tiers may carry affiliated or unknown, which publication surfaces MUST show, so a self-buy cannot masquerade as independent production use.

issuer_counterparty_roles.description: REQUIRED. Every role the issuer played relative to the subject or the observed transactions. An empty array is the issuer's own assertion that it played none of them. It is a claim, not proof: an evaluator MUST NOT treat an empty array at independently_interoperable or above as established independence unless its own accepted-issuer policy records the issuer as a non-participant or the digest-pinned issuance_policy enumerates the issuer's roles and relationships. Omission is not equivalent to empty. Evaluators MUST NOT infer independence from issuer reputation.

items.description: An additional issuer that independently endorses this receipt's claims payload.

counterparty_roles.description: Roles the co-signer declares, with the semantics of issuer_counterparty_roles. A co-signer satisfies the independence requirement only when this array is empty. This copy is a hint: the co-signer's verified credential MUST itself carry its counterparty_roles, and evaluators MUST use the credential's roles, not this copy.

attestation.description: Presentation of the co-signer's own credential. claim_type is a separate endorsement claim so an auditor's own receipt cannot be replayed as an endorsement. The subject is a resource subject: namespace is the receipt issuer's origin, id is this receipt_id, and content_digest is sha256: plus lowercase-hex SHA-256 of UTF8(JCS(this receipt minus co_signers)). The co-signer therefore endorses exactly the issuer's claims, and adding co-signers never changes what is endorsed. attestation.issuer identifies the co-signer. The evaluator verifies the credential exactly as it would any attestation and MUST recompute the digest.

co_signers.description: Independent endorsements of this receipt, at most 8 because each is resolved and verified. Required when evidence_tier is independently_interoperable or above and issuer_counterparty_roles is non-empty, and at least one entry MUST have empty counterparty_roles. The same principal MUST NOT appear twice, and no co-signer may be the issuer, the subject, or the same principal as either.

issuance_policy.description: The conflict-of-interest, appeal, and revocation policy the issuer operated under. REQUIRED at evidence_tier independently_interoperable or above. The policy MUST be published before the first receipt it governs is issued.

uri.description: HTTPS location of the published policy.

content_digest.description: Digest of the exact policy bytes in force at issuance, so a later policy change cannot rewrite what governed this receipt.

publication.description: What the subject agreed to make public. Nothing beyond the fields of this receipt is public by default.

enumDescriptions.private: Disclosed only to the subject and parties it authorizes.
enumDescriptions.public_projection: The subject approved this receipt as a public projection of a richer private record.

consent_digest.description: Digest of the issuer-retained consent record.

party.description: Identity of a party other than the subject named in the claim.

named_parties.description: Other parties this receipt names. Absent by default: a receipt does not identify counterparties. A named party requires that party's own consent; the issuer retains the consent record and a receipt naming a party without it is invalid.

issued_at.description: When the issuer signed the receipt.

expires_at.description: After this instant the receipt MUST NOT be relied on. Receipts are dated evidence, not standing status. MUST be after issued_at.

supersedes.description: receipt_id values, scoped to the same issuer, that this receipt replaces. A superseded receipt is no longer current even before its expires_at. Revocation uses the attestation credential's own issuer-bound status, not this field.

allOf.description: conformance_passed and sandbox_interoperable are sandbox evidence.
independently_interoperable is sandbox or controlled-pilot evidence; production tiers need production.
Independence applies from independently_interoperable upward: a published policy and a counterparty_relation are required, and the issuer cannot declare itself the subject's operator or affiliate.
A non-empty role declaration at independently_interoperable or above requires an independent co-signer.
Lifecycle stages must be backed by the tasks that produce them.

enumDescriptions.subject_operator: The party operates the subject implementation.
enumDescriptions.subject_affiliate: The party is owned by, controls, or is under common control with the subject's operator, or has a revenue-share or exclusive commercial arrangement with it.
enumDescriptions.issuer_affiliate: The party is owned by, controls, or is under common control with the receipt issuer, or has a revenue-share or exclusive commercial arrangement with it. Meaningful for co-signers; an issuer does not declare itself.
enumDescriptions.transaction_counterparty: The party was a party (buyer, seller, or their agent) to the observed transactions.
enumDescriptions.network_intermediary: The party carried, routed, brokered, or observed the transactions as a commercial intermediary. A party that observes AdCP calls because they pass through its infrastructure is a network_intermediary, whatever its neutrality policy.
enumDescriptions.compensated_by_issuer_or_subject: The party is paid by the receipt issuer or the subject for this endorsement or for the observation it covers. Fees from a neutral pool or a pre-published schedule that neither the issuer nor the subject controls do not count.
